title: Automated cutover playbooks with readiness scoring and prefetch probes
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Implement an automated, auditable cutover playbook that 1) computes a per-region readiness index, 2) runs lightweight prefetch probes to warm model KV caches and validate kernel compatibility, and 3) executes a staged cutover with tier-aware routing and deterministic fallback to compatible model variants. This ticket produces the orchestration controller changes, probe scripts, runbook updates, and an initial dashboard for readiness metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Readiness index metric is computed every 30s for each region and surfaces in Console runtime dashboard
Prefetch probe job can be scheduled per-region and returns success/failure plus latency and kv-warmth score
Controller will only promote standby region when readiness_index >= 0.85 and kv_warmth >= 0.7
Cutover performs phased traffic shift (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with automated rollback on error thresholds
Fallback variant matrix enforced: for each model family, controller supports N+1 compatible variants and swaps transparently on missing capacity
Runbook and playbook are documented and linked from the on-call pager flow
technical_design: Readiness Index = weighted(sum) of: node_liveness(0.25), avg_inflight_latency_zscore(0.25), kv_warmth(0.2), kernel_compat_rate(0.15), capacity_headroom(0.15)
kv_warmth measured by prefetch probe: run 4 representative prompts, measure token generation latency, kv_cache_hit_ratio, and compute normalized kv_warmth in [0,1]

Probe implementation: sidecarless probe job that uses the same model image with runtime flags for dry-run and KV-only hot paths; returns structured JSON (status, kv_warmth, latency_ms, kernel_score, details_url)

Tier routing rules: traffic routing table includes priority tiers (gold/silver/free). During failover, gold routes must reach readiness_index threshold 10% earlier and get allocation bias in phased promotion

Variant fallback: model variants registered with compatibility labels (arch:attn-type, quantization:bits) and a compatibility score; controller picks highest-compat variant with available capacity and least expected latency uplift
Cutover smoothing: use a PID-like controller to decide next phase target percentage based on error budget consumption and failed request rate hysteresis
Safety gates: circuit-breaker trips when 5xx rate > 1.5% OR 95th latency > 2x baseline, triggers immediate 50% rollback and re-run probe loop before repeating promotion
